query: In high-entropy alloys, what governs superconducting behavior and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, identify a controlled comparison against a baseline that could reveal the governing cause, predict the relative observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, define its boundary conditions, state what prior evidence would make it plausible, and specify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In single-phase body-centered-cubic high-entropy alloys (bcc HEAs), the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) is governed primarily by the average valence-electron concentration (VEC); Tc reaches a maximum when VEC ≈ 6.8 e⁄atom because the Fermi level coincides with a peak in the electronic density of states (a van-Hove–like singularity), which enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant λ.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic (or near-equiatomic) five-element bcc HEA solid solution composed of early transition metals (e.g., Nb-Ta-Mo-W-V).
generation.intervention: Adjust global composition by isoelectronic substitution (e.g., incrementally replace V (VEC = 5) with Ta (VEC = 5) or Mo (VEC = 6) with Re (VEC = 7) to tune the average VEC from 6.4 to 7.2 while keeping the bcc solid solution intact and maintaining comparable atomic-size misfits.
generation.conditions: Samples arc-melted, homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h, then water-quenched; measurements carried out at ambient pressure from 300 K down to 1.8 K in zero magnetic field for Tc determination (and to 0.3 K for specific-heat measurements).
generation.structural_mediator: Electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), which is modulated by band filling as VEC changes.
generation.mechanism: Tuning VEC shifts the Fermi level through the bcc d-band structure. When EF approaches a van-Hove peak near 6.8 e⁄atom, N(EF) rises, increasing λ = N(EF)⟨I2⟩/M⟨ω2⟩ (McMillan formula). The stronger electron-phonon coupling outweighs disorder scattering, raising Tc. Away from this VEC, N(EF) and λ fall, lowering Tc.
generation.predicted_outcome: A dome-shaped Tc(VEC) curve: Tc rises from ~4 K at VEC ≈ 6.4 to a maximum of ~8 K at VEC ≈ 6.8, then declines to ~3 K at VEC ≈ 7.2. Specific-heat γ and tunneling-derived λ will track the same trend, peaking at VEC ≈ 6.8.
generation.baseline: Composition with VEC ≈ 6.4 (e.g., Nb20Ta20Mo20W20V20) showing Tc ≈ 4 K and lower γ.
generation.boundary: Applies only to single-phase bcc HEAs with 6 ≤ VEC ≤ 7.5, negligible magnetic impurities (< 0.1 at %), and mean free paths shorter than the coherence length (dirty limit). Outside this range (e.g., fcc HEAs or magnetically ordered alloys) the relationship may break down.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of Tc enhancement (factor ~2) is estimated; atomic-scale disorder or local chemical short-range order could dampen the expected peak. Van-Hove singularity position may shift with lattice distortion, broadening the dome.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a compositional series of five samples with VEC = 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 7.0, 7.2 (confirmed by EDS and XRD to be single-phase bcc). Measure (i) Tc via four-probe resistivity and AC susceptibility, (ii) electronic specific-heat coefficient γ at 0.3–5 K, and (iii) electron-phonon coupling λ from low-temperature specific heat fitting.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if Tc, γ, and λ do not show a pronounced maximum (≥20 % higher than adjacent compositions) near VEC ≈ 6.8, or if Tc varies monotonically with VEC without a peak.
